newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit eases vs dlr as interest rates, swaps fall.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit eases vs dlr as interest rates, swaps fall.

text.p: * Ringgit eases as swaps, interest rates return to normalcy after two weeks of turbulence
* Month-end demand for dollars, squaring up by overseas funds pulls down Malaysian unit
* Dollar/ringgit expected to stay in 2.4950/5100 range
The ringgit eased against the dollar in Tuesday morning Asian trading as interbank swaps and interest rates fell, dealers said.
"The swaps are back to normal and so are the interbank rates," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said the markets had calmed down after the interest rate rises caused by an aggressive central bank intervention to prevent the ringgit's fall two weeks ago.
Bank Negara Malaysia is estimated to have sold over $1.0 billion, which sharply reduced domestic market liquidity.
"So people are squaring up their positions," he said.
Dealers said forward rates were once again trading at a discount to the domestic interest rates, which was the case before the turbulence began.

One-month swaps were quoting at 35/40 points, which translated into an impact rate of 7.3/4 percent, dealers said. A few days ago one-month had touched a high of 500, which implied a yield of 20 percent.
In the domestic market the one-month rate went up to as high as 9.5 percent last week. On Tuesday, one-month money was trading at 7.5/8.0 percent.
Some dealers said the fall in rates also combined with month-end commercial dollar demand from Kuala Lumpur to push up dollar/ringgit.

"Dollar/ringgit should be in a wide range of 2.4950/5100 in the near-term, but towards the higher side of the range, as not many have to desire to be long ringgit," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
At 0220 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5045/55 to a dollar.
